issues.title: Perfect HT: fused single-pass update for int64 sum/avg/count_star aggregates
issues.hypothesis: PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY is still 1.32s CPU of ~2.7s query CPU on q01 (profile.md). It runs 8 aggregates x 58.8M rows = ~470M state updates, about 2.8ns each. Each aggregate takes its own pass: RowOperations::UpdateStates -> ToUnifiedFormat on a dictionary-sliced payload (the scan filter slices every column), then a scatter loop that reloads the state pointer and goes through sel indirection, and then AddInPlace on the address vector. E0001 and E0003 showed the per-pass scatter itself is the remaining cost, not dependency chains (the E0003 notes suggest fusing). A single row loop that loads the group address once and updates all the int64 states of the tuple (2 adjacent cache lines) removes 7 of the 8 address reloads, 8 AddInPlace passes and per-aggregate dispatch. The update count stays the same, but the work per update should drop by ~2x.
issues.plan: In src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp (+ .hpp): in the constructor, classify every aggregate in layout_ptr->GetAggregates(). The fused path is enabled only if ALL aggregates are unfiltered, non-distinct and one of: (a) count_star (child_count 0, state int64 counter); (b) sum_no_overflow with input physical type INT32/INT64 (state SumState<int64_t>: isset + value; check that state_size matches); (c) avg whose state is AvgState<int64_t> (from E0004: input physical INT32/INT64 and state_size == sizeof(AvgState<int64_t>) = 16; the hugeint state is larger, so state_size tells them apart; double avg must be excluded by requiring an integer physical input type). Before writing the classification, read the exact state structs in extension/core_functions/include/core_functions/aggregate/sum_helpers.hpp and avg.cpp and record the field offsets; if their layout is not reachable from src/, mirror it with static_asserted local structs. In AddChunk, after the address loop, if fused: ToUnifiedFormat each payload column once, then one loop over rows i: base = address_data[i]; for each aggregate k (small array of {kind, offset, payload col}): idx = sel_k->get_index(i); if valid, update state at base+offset_k (sum: isset=true, value+=v; avg: count++, value+=v; count_star: ++). Treat NULLs exactly as the existing ops do (sum/avg skip NULLs; count_star counts all). A templated inner loop for the case where no payload column has a validity mask is worthwhile. Otherwise use the existing per-aggregate path. Combine/Scan/finalize are unchanged because the state layouts are unchanged. Keep the E0003 replica logic.
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY with a small group domain (perfect HT) over integer/decimal(<=18) sum/avg/count, which is very common in analytical reporting queries. Other aggregate mixes are unaffected and fall back to the existing path.
issues.risk: Medium: mismatched state layouts would give wrong results, so use static_asserts and state_size checks. NULL handling must match. Falling back for anything unrecognised keeps the risk contained.

issues.title: Perfect HT: replica count 8
issues.hypothesis: E0003 K=4 cut HT CPU 1.50->1.37s. With 4 skewed groups (49% in one) and 2-cache-line tuples, 8 replicas may hide more store-to-load latency. It is cheap to try.
issues.plan: Change MAX_REPLICA_COUNT in src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp from 4 to 8, keeping the 1MiB size cap.
issues.risk: Low; possible small slowdown for larger group domains due to cache footprint (capped).

dispatch: Perfect HT: fused single-pass update for int64 sum/avg/count_star aggregates
output.memory:
# Memory

## Workload
- Single visible template q01 = TPC-H Q1 shape: scan lineitem with one range filter on a date (selects ~98%),
  4 groups (2 string keys -> compressed to utinyint), 4 sum_no_overflow + 3 avg + count_star on DECIMAL(int64).
- Bench ~314-337ms after E0004. Operator CPU (profile): TABLE_SCAN ~2.00s, PERFECT_HASH_GROUP_BY ~1.32s,
  projections 0.20 + 0.04 + 0.18s.
- Storage (pragma_storage_info): l_quantity/extendedprice/discount/tax/shipdate = BitPacking; returnflag/linestatus = Dictionary
  (old dictionary compression, 978 segments, ~61K rows each). The old dictionary scan emits DictionaryVector (decompression.cpp:98).
- Types: l_* decimals DECIMAL(15,2) int64; sums run as sum_no_overflow (int64 state); avg is now an int64 state via E0004.
- Group distribution: N,O 49%, A,F 25%, R,F 25%, N,F <1% -> skewed, randomly interleaved.

## Key measurements (dbe-tool sql, single runs, noisy; ~6-8ns/value/column CPU everywhere)
- Q1 with filter ~680ms; no filter ~480ms; no filter + max(l_shipdate) ~555ms -> filter path costs >=18%.
- count(*) with only the date filter: 71ms; adding 4 more trivial filters on the decimal cols: 265ms.
- sum of 4 decimal cols, no filter 225ms, with date filter 350ms.
- group by returnflag,linestatus count(*): ~180-207ms; group by 1 key: 134ms.
- HT: ~470M state updates at ~2.8ns each.

## Codebase facts
- Scan with filters: RowGroup::Scan (src/storage/table/row_group.cpp ~694-829). Filter cols -> StandardColumnData::Filter
  (standard_column_data.cpp:76): compression->filter if present, else Scan + ToUnifiedFormat + FilterSelection.
  Other cols -> compression->select if present, else full Scan + Slice(sel).
- Compression funcs with select: constant, RLE, dict_fsst, validity. No bitpacking filter/select.
- fixed_size_uncompressed scan is zero-copy -> never compact scan results in place generically.
- Perfect hash agg: src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp. AddChunk (l.137): ComputeGroupLocation per key,
  bounds check + group_is_set + replica address (l.154-164), then per aggregate UpdateStates + AddInPlace (l.170-182).
  CombineReplicas folds replicas. MAX_REPLICA_COUNT constant at top of file.
- sum_no_overflow: extension/core_functions/aggregate/distributive/sum.cpp (l.90-122, 294).
- Statistics rewrite hook: AggregateFunction statistics callback, called from
  src/optimizer/statistics/expression/propagate_aggregate.cpp (SumPropagateStats sum.cpp:126; AvgPropagateStats in avg.cpp from E0004).
- Scatter loops: src/include/duckdb/common/vector_operations/aggregate_executor.hpp.
- dbe-tool sql: selecting typeof(col) without an aggregate errors; wrap it in any_value(). EXPLAIN ANALYZE works.
  Bash: only plain dbe-tool calls.

## Round log
- G1R1: E0001 per-group simple_update in perfect HT -> RETIRED (bad idea: groups interleaved, partitioning costs more).
- G1R2: E0002 bitpacking select (flat compacted payload) -> RETIRED: neutral. Slicing is not the cost.
- G1R3: E0003 perfect HT replicate states K=4 -> ACCEPTED, -12.3% (1.140x).
- G1R4: E0004 avg int64 state via stats -> ACCEPTED, -5.1% (1.201x).
- G1R5: dispatched "Perfect HT: fused single-pass update for int64 sum/avg/count_star aggregates"
  (classify aggregates by name/state_size/input physical type; one row loop updates all states; fall back otherwise).

## Ideas not yet explored / backlog
- Perfect HT K=8 replicas (filed, cheap).
- Fuse stacked projections (backlog; needs investigation of compressed_materialization). ~0.42s CPU in projections.
- Bitpacking `filter` callback (filter while decompressing). The date filter alone costs 71ms, so the gain is limited.
- Decimal multiply overflow checks in projections (could skip using stats).
- Scan is the largest operator (2.0s, ~5ns/value); no single anomaly found yet. Old Dictionary select callback is untried.
